q: Under which provision of law did the RBI introduce the Banking Ombudsman Scheme?
options: Section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949
explain: The scheme was introduced by the RBI under Section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949. Section 45L of the RBI Act is the basis of the NBFC scheme.

q: Who appoints the Banking Ombudsman?
explain: The Banking Ombudsman is a senior official appointed by the Reserve Bank of India, not by the Government or any bank.

q: The Banking Ombudsman is appointed for which purpose?
options: Redressing customers’ complaints about deficiency in certain banking services
Deciding CRR, SLR and MSF rates
Handling banks’ complaints against customers’ behaviour
explain: The Ombudsman deals with customers’ complaints about deficiency in certain banking services. Monetary policy tools like CRR and SLR are set by the RBI itself.

q: Which version of the Banking Ombudsman Scheme was in operation (as amended up to 1 July 2017) before the 2021 integrated scheme?
explain: The Banking Ombudsman Scheme 2006, amended up to 1 July 2017, was the version in operation. The 2018 scheme is the separate NBFC scheme.

q: The Banking Ombudsman Scheme was first introduced by the RBI with effect from which year?
explain: The scheme began in 1995 and was later revised; the 2006 version is the one that stayed in operation for years.

q: The Banking Ombudsman Scheme 2006 is applicable to the business of which banks?
options: Scheduled commercial banks including RRBs, and scheduled primary co-operative banks
explain: The scheme covers all scheduled commercial banks, Regional Rural Banks and scheduled primary co-operative banks.

q: Which of the following is NOT covered by the Banking Ombudsman Scheme 2006?
explain: The scheme covers scheduled commercial banks, RRBs and scheduled primary co-operative banks. Insurance companies are outside it.

q: Who is a Banking Ombudsman?
options: The chief vigilance officer of a bank
An official in the Finance Ministry
A senior official appointed by the RBI to address customer complaints
explain: A Banking Ombudsman is a senior official appointed by the RBI to redress customer complaints about certain bank services.

q: As per the source, how many Banking Ombudsmen had been appointed, with offices mostly in state capitals?
explain: At the time of writing, 20 Banking Ombudsmen were appointed, with offices mostly in state capitals. Such counts can change.

q: Which of the following is a ground for complaint to the Banking Ombudsman (other than loans and advances)?
options: Levying of charges without adequate prior notice to the customer
The bank opening a new branch
A customer disliking the branch interior
explain: Levying charges without adequate prior notice is a listed service deficiency. The other options are not service deficiencies.

q: Which of the following is a ground of complaint related to loans and advances under the 2006 scheme?
options: Share price fall of the bank
Delay in sanction or disbursement beyond the prescribed time schedule
A branch closing on a public holiday
explain: Delay in sanction or disbursement, or ignoring the prescribed time schedule for loan applications, is a listed ground. Bank share prices and dividends are not.

q: Whose complaints about remittances from abroad, deposits and other bank matters can be taken to the Banking Ombudsman?
explain: The scheme lists complaints from NRIs having accounts in India about remittances from abroad, deposits and other bank-related matters.

q: Which of these can be taken to the Banking Ombudsman?
options: Refusal to open a deposit account without a valid reason
A dispute about a company’s share allotment
A wish for lower income tax
A complaint about a stock broker’s fees
explain: Refusal to open a deposit account without valid reason is a listed deficiency in banking service. The other items belong to other forums.

q: A customer may approach the Banking Ombudsman if the bank has not replied within how long of receiving the complaint?
explain: The customer can go to the Ombudsman if there is no reply within one month, or the complaint is rejected, or the reply is unsatisfactory.

q: Which of the following is NOT a situation that lets a customer approach the Banking Ombudsman?
options: No reply from the bank after one month
The customer is not satisfied with the bank’s reply
The customer has not complained to the bank at all
explain: The bank must be approached first. Only no reply in one month, rejection, or dissatisfaction with the reply opens the Ombudsman route.

q: The Ombudsman Scheme for NBFCs came into effect on 23 February of which year?
explain: The NBFC Ombudsman Scheme came into effect on 23 February 2018, under Section 45L of the RBI Act, 1934.

q: The Ombudsman Scheme for NBFCs, 2018 was introduced under which section?
options: Section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949
Section 29A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951
explain: The NBFC scheme rests on Section 45L of the RBI Act, 1934. Section 35A of the BR Act is the basis of the Banking Ombudsman Scheme.

q: Where are the offices of the NBFC Ombudsman located?
explain: NBFC Ombudsman offices are in Chennai, Kolkata, New Delhi and Mumbai, the four metros.

q: Which NBFCs were covered first under the NBFC Ombudsman Scheme 2018?
options: Only NBFCs listed on stock exchanges
explain: The scheme initially covered NBFCs authorised to accept deposits, to be extended gradually to other identified NBFCs.

q: Besides deposit-taking NBFCs, NBFCs with customer interface are covered by the 2018 scheme if their asset size is at least:
explain: One billion rupees equals ₹100 crore, which is the asset size threshold for NBFCs with customer interface.

q: What is the cap on compensation for loss under the NBFC Ombudsman Scheme?
options: The direct loss or ₹10 lakh, whichever is lower
explain: Compensation for loss is limited to the amount arising directly from the NBFC’s act or omission, or ₹10 lakh (one million), whichever is lower.

q: What is the maximum extra compensation the NBFC Ombudsman may award for mental agony and harassment?
explain: The NBFC Ombudsman can award up to ₹1 lakh (0.1 million) for mental agony and harassment.

q: Which of the following is a ground for complaint to the NBFC Ombudsman?
options: A delay in releasing securities or documents after the borrower repays all dues
The NBFC opening a new branch
A borrower refusing to repay the loan
explain: Failure or inordinate delay in releasing securities or documents after repayment of all dues is a listed ground.

q: Under the NBFC scheme, the sanction letter and terms must be provided in:
options: A vernacular language, or a language the borrower understands
explain: Failure to give the sanction letter and terms in a vernacular language or one understood by the borrower is a ground of complaint.

q: A complaint against an NBFC goes to which NBFC Ombudsman?
options: The one in the complainant’s home town
The one whose jurisdiction covers the NBFC’s branch or registered office
explain: The complaint is filed with the NBFC Ombudsman under whose jurisdiction the NBFC’s branch or registered office falls, after first approaching the NBFC.

q: Within how many days of receiving the award or rejection can an appeal be filed against the NBFC Ombudsman’s decision?
explain: An appeal must be filed within 30 days of receiving the communication of the award or rejection.

q: If sufficient cause is shown, the Appellate Authority may allow a further period of not more than how many days to appeal?
explain: A further period not exceeding 30 days may be allowed if the applicant had sufficient cause for the delay.

q: Which of the following is NOT a power of the Appellate Authority under the NBFC scheme?
explain: The Appellate Authority can dismiss, set aside, send back for fresh disposal, modify the award or pass any other order. Cancelling registration is not among them.

q: With reference to NBFCs in India, consider: (1) They cannot accept demand deposits like a savings account. (2) They are not allowed to open savings bank accounts and are not members of the clearing houses. (3) They cannot acquire securities issued by the government. Which are correct?
explain: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. NBFCs can acquire government securities; it is part of their business, so statement 3 is wrong.

q: A minimum of what percentage of the total assets of an IFC-NBFC must be deployed in infrastructure loans?
explain: An Infrastructure Finance Company NBFC must deploy at least 75% of its total assets in infrastructure loans.

q: Which of the following can an NBFC do, unlike a bank?
options: Accept deposits only in forms such as fixed deposits, not as demand deposits
Become a member of the clearing house
explain: NBFCs may take term-type deposits like fixed deposits but cannot accept demand deposits, open savings accounts or join clearing houses.

q: Which three schemes were merged into the RBI’s Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2021?
options: Banking Ombudsman 2006, NBFC 2018 and Digital Transactions 2019
explain: RB-IOS 2021 merged the Banking Ombudsman Scheme 2006, the NBFC Ombudsman Scheme 2018 and the Ombudsman Scheme for Digital Transactions 2019.

q: Under the RBI Integrated Ombudsman Scheme 2021, the Ombudsman can award compensation for direct loss up to:
explain: The 2021 scheme allows up to ₹20 lakh for direct loss, plus up to ₹1 lakh for loss of time, harassment and mental agony.

q: Where is the Centralised Receipt and Processing Centre (CRPC) of the Integrated Ombudsman Scheme located?
explain: The CRPC that receives and processes complaints under the Integrated Ombudsman Scheme is at Chandigarh.

q: Under the Integrated Ombudsman Scheme 2021, how long does the regulated entity get to reply before the customer can escalate?
explain: The regulated entity has 30 days to reply, after which the complaint can go to the Ombudsman.

q: The Integrated Ombudsman Scheme replaced fixed lists of grounds with which general ground?
explain: RB-IOS 2021 follows a One Nation, One Ombudsman approach, with complaints accepted for deficiency in service rather than only listed grounds.
